text: But only if you finish the treatment.
Six months. One hundred and eighty mornings. Every single dose.
Patients often feel better within weeks, and that is when doses start to slip.
In Indonesia, every patient has a treatment supervisor, a P.M.O. But no supervisor can be there every morning.
So we built a companion that is.
It knows who is taking the medicine.
It reads the pulse and oxygen level through a light-sealed finger sensor.
Inside, the original blister moves down, row by row, like bread in a toaster.
A small plunger presses one caplet through the foil. Never more. Never less.
Seconds later, the supervisor knows. Dose taken. Verified.
Day forty-seven. One hundred and thirty-three to go.
